answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust grow like a meadow: slowly, from many small tended contributions, and withers if untended, so a fresh identity cannot buy standing in a day. Every claim passes through a prism, split into separate facets — who did the work, when, and what changed — each checked by a different peer, so a forged claim fails at least one facet. Newcomers enter only through one narrow inlet, a public probation queue where first jobs are inspected openly, and a sudden burst of identical fresh accounts is easy to spot and freeze before any rewards flow.
